Carnality is the state or condition of being heavily absorbed in, or driven by, the desires of the physical body — especially sexual desire — rather than the mind or spirit.

Think of a human being as having three layers:

  • The body (physical, instinctive, animal)
  • The mind (rational, intellectual)
  • The spirit (moral, ethical, divine)

Carnality is when the body layer dominates. It's the condition of living as though physical urges — particularly sexual ones — are the most important force guiding your thoughts, choices, and actions.

Imagine a spectrum. On one end, you have pure spirituality — a person completely devoted to God, virtue, or the life of the mind, with little interest in bodily pleasures. On the other end, you have pure carnality — a person entirely consumed by physical urges, especially lust, with little regard for morality, self-control, or spiritual values.

Carnality is the quality of being on that far end — or of moving toward it. It is not just having physical desires (which is normal and human), but being ruled by them, letting them override everything else.
The Two Contexts Where This Word Is Used

1. Sexual / Physical Desire

This is the most common everyday use. When someone speaks of "carnality," they most often mean raw, intense sexual desire — the part of human nature that is driven purely by physical appetite, with no filtering by love, morality, or emotional connection.

For example, a relationship built purely on carnality is one driven entirely by physical attraction and sexual urge — not by emotional bond, respect, or spiritual connection.

2. Religious and Moral Context

In religious traditions — especially Christianity — carnality has a deeper, broader meaning. It refers to the sinful, earthly nature of human beings: the tendency to prioritize the pleasures and concerns of this physical world (sex, greed, self-indulgence, material comfort) over God, virtue, and the soul.

In this context, carnality is almost the opposite of holiness. A "carnal" person, in religious language, is someone still under the control of their sinful, worldly impulses — someone who has not yet submitted themselves to spiritual discipline or divine will.

This is why the Bible, for example, contrasts the "carnal mind" (one fixated on worldly things) with the "spiritual mind" (one aligned with God). Carnality, in this sense, is not just about sex — it's about any attachment to the earthly and physical over the eternal and divine.

• It is not simply having a physical body or physical desires. Every human being does, and that alone is not carnality.
  • It is not just one sexual act or one moment of desire. That might be called a carnal act, but carnality (as a noun) refers to a broader state, pattern, or quality — a defining orientation of a person's nature.
  • It is not a neutral word. It almost always carries a negative or at least serious tone — a sense of something excessive, unchecked, or morally questionable.
The Tone and Register of the Word

Carnality is a formal, serious word. You will find it in:

  • Religious texts and sermons
  • Literary fiction (especially classic literature)
  • Philosophical writing
  • Serious discussions of human nature, morality, or sexuality

You would not hear it in casual conversation. No one says, "I felt a lot of carnality last weekend." The word carries weight. It suggests a deep, often troubling dominance of physical appetite over reason, conscience, or spirit.

• "The monk devoted his life to God, struggling daily against the carnality that tempted him."

→ Here, carnality means the pull of bodily and sexual desires that fight against spiritual devotion.

  • "The novel explored the carnality of the affair — two people driven purely by physical hunger with no emotional tenderness between them."

→ Here, carnality means raw, unrestrained sexual desire with no deeper connection.

  • "The preacher warned his congregation that carnality — the love of worldly pleasures — was the great enemy of the soul."

→ Here, carnality is the broader religious sense: attachment to earthly things over spiritual ones.

Carnality is the state of being ruled by the body's raw physical desires — especially sexual ones — at the expense of the mind, morality, or spirit.

It is the condition of the person who lives downward, into instinct and flesh, rather than upward, into reason and soul.
